findings.discovered_in: Unfrozen source construction; original source bytes were not retained by reviewer. No failed runtime observation claimed.
findings.problem: A deadline-exceeded effect removed the local reservation; shutdown inferred completed for every absent inventory entry, mislabeling the durable failed deadline as useful completion.
findings.repair: Record explicit completed/deadline-exceeded outcomes; unresolved fallback; propagate rejected release reasons.
findings.observed_regression: durable_deadlines_and_local_budget: actual SIGTERM at before_effect seam, persisted deadline expiry, rejected effect, shutdown disposition deadline-exceeded, zero progress/receipts/total and no completed_at.
findings.verification: Passed in independent frozen CLI; source semantics independently reviewed.

findings.discovered_in: Source analysis of a valid pending full checkpoint; original 7-case author snapshot did not exercise this boundary.
findings.problem: Claim admitted checkpoint == len(manifest), but the next slice indexed past the input rather than finishing. A crash after the final checkpoint and before terminal completion could leave complete effects permanently pending through the runtime.
findings.repair: Immediately perform guarded finish for a restored full cursor, with no input indexing or new effect; verifier expects the completion event.
findings.observed_regression: final_checkpoint_before_completion: actual SIGKILL after acknowledged final checkpoint but before finish; pending checkpoint 1, one receipt, total 4 and no completed_at; v2 resumes and finalizes with unchanged receipt/total.
findings.verification: Passed in independent frozen CLI; source semantics independently reviewed.

limitations: Bounded slices represent 12/24-hour jobs; no endurance, Kubernetes, scheduler, or orchestrator test.
Effects, receipts, checkpoints and epoch fencing share one PostgreSQL database; no external provider or broker guarantee.
v1/v2 are distinct entrypoints with differing input interpreters over a shared runtime/protocol, not independently released production binaries.
Ownership uses a two-second fixture lease without renewal; only the budget scenario waits for natural expiry. Other expiry schedules are fixture mutations.
The first-SIGTERM monotonic budget stops new slices and bounds cooperative waits. SQL has per-statement/lock bounds; this is not a strict cumulative transaction or commit deadline.
Persisted job deadlines reject decisions after database-time expiry; effects admitted before expiry can commit afterward.
Admission ordering covers committed-before-local-publication and post-gate-close rejection; no exhaustive concurrent admission stress test.
PostgreSQL tmpfs has fsync and synchronous_commit on, but no power-loss, restore, partition, database crash or failover evidence.
Prefetch is a leased local database reservation, not a broker delivery/redelivery budget. Control barriers run outside protected transactions.

independent_observational_checks.source_report_bindings: All 10 current file hashes match author and independent reports before/after execution. Author verification and both historical report byte hashes unchanged.
independent_observational_checks.fixture_ledger_method: Manually specified fixture amounts and interpretation tuples; Python standard JSON/hash arithmetic only, without importing protocol.amounts or other implementation functions.
independent_observational_checks.admission_race_limit: Its final row is not returned in the report; final-state assertion is observed through the executed bound verifier, not separately recalculated from a published row.
independent_observational_checks.first_signal_budgets: Six retirement events retain deadline=first signal+1; short-budget case retains first signal+.2 after a repeated SIGTERM. These are observed cooperative bounds with margins, not strict arbitrary SQL/commit or kernel delivery guarantees.

postflight.method: OS existence check on each published PID, loopback connection attempts for each published listener and docker container ls exact run-id filter; no unowned resource cleanup.

independent_observational_checks.legacy_unchanged: git diff --quiet -- examples/draining returned0; legacy runtime was not rerun.

technical_assessment.signal_and_admission: Minimal main-thread SIGTERM handler preserves first monotonic deadline; runtime closes DB generation gate and reconciles accepted claims from durable ownership, including committed-before-local-publication and prefetched work. Actual readiness/admission events observed.
technical_assessment.fencing_and_receipts: Job FOR UPDATE plus owner/epoch/input guard remain inside the same transaction as receipt/business-total mutation. Live resumed stale owner rejects effect/checkpoint/release. Receipt gap recovery keeps original operation identity; this protects database-owned effects only.
technical_assessment.compatibility: Named v1 tuple is retained by v2; structured v2 input is also executed; unsupported tuple blocks ownership mutation; immutable DB trigger protects input/hash/schemas/semantics. Shared runtime/implementation limits remain explicit.
technical_assessment.deadlines: Persisted database-time business deadline survives replacements and remains separate from first-signal monotonic drain budget. Expiry is terminal, not useful completion or business retry. Admission before expiry may commit afterward; no strict commit deadline inferred.
technical_assessment.useful_completion: Clean worker exits are separated from durable logical completion. Baseline exhausts3 business failures at checkpoint 3/total 6; protected main completes 6 steps/total 21 with 0 business failures, and all 3 returned prefetch jobs complete. Final-checkpoint recovery reaches terminal state without new effect.
technical_assessment.cleanup: Run-owned process groups, control streams, loopback listeners, example database sessions and labeled container have bounded cleanup. Independent postflight confirms reported PIDs/ports/container absence. Session-zero assertions exclude the live observer and filter example application_name; observer closure is then recorded.

actual_read_scope: Reviewer read complete runtime/protocol/schema/verifier, all version entrypoints, README/sources, current author report and earlier report metadata. limits: One short local PostgreSQL/POSIX-process run; no 12/24-hour endurance or Kubernetes/orchestrator run.
No broker receive/redelivery budget or external provider effect contract; prefetch is a durable local DB reservation.
No database power loss, crash/restart, failover, partition, restore, backup or RPO evidence; storage is tmpfs despite fsync/synchronous_commit on.
No general arbitrary release compatibility proof; v1/v2 share runtime/protocol and validate only named interpretation profiles.
Controlled committed-before-publication admission seam and post-close rejection, not exhaustive simultaneous claim/gate stress.
Per-statement/lock SQL limits and observed cooperative shutdown margins do not establish a strict total transaction/commit deadline or immediate kernel signal handling.
No model trial, model/config change, implementation/skill edit, commit, push or publication by this review.
